title: Time Based Key Value Store
description:
Keep timestamped string values under keys and retrieve the value most recently set at or before a query time.

Implement the TimeMap class:

  • __init__() creates an empty store.
  • set(key: str, value: str, timestamp: int) -> None records value under key at timestamp.
  • get(key: str, timestamp: int) -> str returns the value for that key with the greatest stored timestamp not exceeding timestamp, or the empty string when none exists.

Set timestamps for each key arrive in strictly increasing order. Keys are independent, and a get never changes stored data.

You are graded on a recorded sequence of calls on one live object. The first call names the class and passes constructor arguments; subsequent calls name methods and their arguments. The constructor and methods returning nothing report null; the result array has one entry per call.

Constraints:

  • Keys and values contain 1 to 100 lowercase English letters or digits.
  • 1 <= timestamp <= 10000000.
  • At most 200000 calls; get should use binary search rather than scan the entire history.

Example 1:

Calls: ["TimeMap","set","get","get","set","get","get"]
Arguments: [[],["foo","bar",1],["foo",1],["foo",3],["foo","baz",4],["foo",4],["foo",5]]
Output: [null,null,"bar","bar",null,"baz","baz"]

The lookup at 3 uses time 1; after time 4 is stored, later lookups use baz.

Example 2:

Calls: ["TimeMap","set","get","get","set","get"]
Arguments: [[],["a","old",5],["a",4],["a",5],["a","new",9],["a",8]]
Output: [null,null,"","old",null,"old"]

Before time 5 there is no value; a lookup at 8 still uses old.

Example 3:

Calls: ["TimeMap","set","set","get","get","get"]
Arguments: [[],["x","one",2],["y","two",1],["x",1],["y",10],["x",2]]
Output: [null,null,null,"","two","one"]

A value under y does not supply an answer for x.

testCases.explanation: The lookup at 3 uses time 1; after time 4 is stored, later lookups use baz.
Before time 5 there is no value; a lookup at 8 still uses old.
A value under y does not supply an answer for x.
An unknown key has no prior value.
Choose the greatest timestamp not exceeding the requested time.
Timelines for distinct keys do not mix.
A distant future entry cannot answer an earlier lookup.
Later writes do not retroactively change earlier lookups.
Between writes use the first value; before both use the empty string.
